name: indun-map-list-cap
summary: The WorldManager accepts at most 32 instance-dungeon (map, level) rows for the WHOLE world and refuses a registration packet carrying more. Relocate the array and raise the guard, so a 2026 port can host more than 32.
status: BUILT 2026-09-23 from NOTES-map-caps.md section 4; statically verified, NOT yet run by a WorldManager process.
why: The WM does not read Field.txt. Each zone, on its S2S connection ack (FieldContainer::fc_IndunMapRegist,
0x462AF0 in Zone.exe), sends NC_INSTANCE_DUNGEON_MAP_REGIST_CMD with EVERY InstanceDungeon row of its
Field.txt - not only its own zone's - as {MapIDClient[12]; ModeIDLv u8} = 13 bytes each behind a u16 count.
CParserZone::fc_NC_INSTANCE_DUNGEON_MAP_REGIST_CMD (0x428870) then:
0x4288C1  cmp word [esi], 0x20 ; ja fail      <- refuses a packet with more than 32 entries
0x4288C9  cmp [0x557D10], 0 ; jg skip          <- keeps only the FIRST registration, so every zone must
send the complete list (they do)
0x4288E2  mov edx, 0x557D12                    \
0x4288EF  mov edi, 0x557D0E                     | four bases of the strength-reduced copy loop, each
0x4288F4  mov edx, 0x557D0A                     | = m_IndunMapList - 0xA + {0, 4, 8, 12}
0x4288FB  mov ebx, 0x557D16                    /
copying into CWMZoneSessionManager::m_IndunMapList at 0x557D14 - 32 entries of 13 B = 416 bytes - with the
count in m_NumOfIndunMap at 0x557D10, then echoing the list back to the zones (opcode 0xA41A, built in a
0x2014-byte stack buffer that already holds 630 entries).
A reference scan of 0x557D00-0x557EB8 (common/tools/xref_range.py, 2026-09-14) found NOTHING else in the WM
touching the array - only this handler's four bases and the count. So the cap moves with five edits: the
array to a region of its own, and the guard.
WHY 127. The guard is an imm8 in a 16-bit compare (66 83 3E xx), so it sign-extends: 0x7F is the largest
value that stays positive, and a bigger one would read as negative and refuse everything. 127 rows is 1651
bytes. The zone side is already past this (instance-cluster-cap gives 32 clusters per zone process), and the
echo buffer holds 630, so 127 is the whole remaining ceiling.
THE COUNT DOES NOT MOVE. m_NumOfIndunMap stays at 0x557D10; only the array base changes. The old 416 bytes
at 0x557D14 are left where they are - nothing reads them once the four bases point elsewhere.
A ZERO-FILL REGION IS RIGHT for the array: the count starts at 0 and every entry is written before it is
read, exactly as the stock .bss array was.
ALSO NEEDED IN THE DATA (merge rule, from the same reading): the zone stores InstanceDungeon rows in a
pointer array INDEXED BY IDNo (fc_Load: [FieldContainer+0x54078][IDNo]) and fc_IndunMapRegist walks slots
0..rowcount-1, so IDNo must run contiguously from 0 - a row whose IDNo >= rowcount is never registered with
the WM at all, and a gap leaves a null slot the loop skips.
HOW TO PROVE IT: put more than 32 InstanceDungeon rows in a zone's Field.txt, start the WM and that zone, and
read m_NumOfIndunMap (0x557D10) in the live WM - stock refuses the packet and leaves it 0; patched it holds
the row count, and the zones get the echo.
